title: What Happened Was… starring Corey Stoll and Cecily Strong at the Mine...
transcript: This play definitely had me laughing, but mostly crawling out of my skin. New York is a notoriously lonely city, and its dating scene does not have a great reputation. In this two-hander from the 90s by Tom Noonan, coworkers Jackie and Michael are meeting up for the first time outside of the office. Obviously, it's a new experience with its own dynamic, but you'd think they're complete strangers by how painfully awkward it is — it's funny but in a relentlessly uncomfortable way that might even cross into unenjoyable for some. Things do gradually shift, though, and this initial ego dismemberment ends up paying off in a couple of ways. For one, the characters are established efficiently — you learn a lot about the core of who someone is when they're in a vulnerable situation. Secondly, this setup makes their efforts to see and understand each other way more emotionally impactful later in the play. It also helps that Cecily Strong and Corey Stoll are giving wonderful performances that surface themes and nuances from the story that I doubt jump off the page of the script. They are what makes this a beautiful production about how we aren't just extras in each other's stories — we're all layered and lonely in our own ways. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Despite noting the discomfort might be 'unenjoyable for some,' the reviewer ultimately praises it as a 'beautiful production' with 'wonderful performances' and emotionally impactful payoff. The framing is a clear recommendation with a caveat about tone.
